title: 📢 Sept. 28 Annapolis Council: food homes, parking, rentals
text:
1 days ago Annapolis City Council meets on Monday, September 28 at 7 p.m. at City Hall, 160 Duke of Gloucester St. The meeting is open to the public , and you can also watch on YouTube (YouTube.com/CityofAnnapolis) or City of Annapolis TV (Verizon 99/100, Comcast 34) .
Key items on the agenda:
Art in Public Places Commission : Council will consider the first 5 nominees for the reconstituted commission and is still seeking applicants from other wards. Public hearing – O-15-26 Cottage Food Businesses : Would let residents run certain home-based food businesses (baked goods, jams, candies) that don’t need refrigeration. First Readers (early discussion stage): Parking districts lettering (O-26-26) – rename special residential parking districts from numbers to letters. Water line right of entry (O-27-26) – let the City enter private property to inspect/replace water lines. Transportation fine waivers (O-28-26) – allow some transportation fines to be waived. Outdoor dining rules update (O-29-26) – update standards, including barrier design. Main Street Advisory Task Force (R-34-26) – create a temporary citizen task force. Water service for 3020 Arundel on the Bay Rd. (R-35-26) – extend City water to property outside City limits. Second Readers (discussion, public testimony, and possible votes): Right to park in front of your own driveway (O-17-26) . AiPPC restructuring extension (O-22-26) . Collective bargaining agreements (R-24-26, R-25-26, R-26-26) for AFSCME Local 3406 , IAFF Local 1926 , and UFCW Local 400 (Police) for FY 2027–2028 . Fee waiver up to $20,000 for the 2026 Freedom Mortgage Military Bowl Parade (R-28-26) . Higher fines for short-term rental violations (R-33-26) . You can testify in person at City Hall or submit online testimony on these specific bills.
